 Jimmy Fallon Mocks Trump Officials Over FAA Outage Chaos In Humiliating Skit
 The late-night host joked that America’s planes are apparently “run by the same technology as the Chuck E. Cheese Band.”
 By   Jazmin Tolliver Trends Reporter, HuffPost
 Nov 16, 2026, 09:06 PM EST Leave a Comment LOADING ERROR LOADING Jimmy Fallon mocked Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin for their response to Friday’s Federal Aviation Administration outage, which sparked chaos and disrupted airline schedules nationwide. 
 “Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the issue was caused by old switches, old routers and copper lines from the 1980s,” he said Sunday on “The Tonight Show.” “ Apparently our planes are run by the same technology as the Chuck E. Cheese Band.” 
 Advertisement 
 Fallon then played a clip of Duffy’s Nov. 14 press conference. Duffy tried to address the press, but he kept getting interrupted by a high-pitched feedback sound. 
 “I just want to first start off by extending my gratitude for what happened yesterday and the amazing performance of our air-traffic controllers,” Duffy said as the noise persisted. 
 Duffy paused, then said, “We’ll wait a second here,” but the humming sound continued. 
 When the clip ended, Fallon joked, “Well, I feel better. That pretty much explains the FAA’s new slogan: ‘What the FAA?!’” 
 Advertisement 
 A faux Duffy and Mullin then joined Fallon to discuss the sweeping ground stop that caused thousands of flights to be canceled or delayed. The two impersonators parodied an actual press conference Duffy and Mullin held at the White House on Friday in the wake of the outage, where they said the ground stop was caused by a temporary telecommunications and data-overload issues. 
 When Fallon asked if the FAA outage had anything to do with the Microsoft Outlook outage that happened a day earlier, the Duffy imitator confessed he was clueless about both. 
 “We don’t know, Jimmy. I mean, people have tried explaining it to us, but we don’t understand a word they’re saying,” the mock Duffy replied. 
 Advertisement 
 “They’re both computers,” the faux Mullin chimed in. “We’re 99% sure about that. Except one of them’s for airplanes and one of them’s for emails.” 
 The FAA ended the nationwide ground stop at approximately 8:15 p.m. ET on Friday after more than 4 hours of disruption. But travel delays continued throughout the weekend.
